name: linux-docs-deploy
title: Linux host docs, systemd unit and Dockerfile
issue: Approved by the user 2026-10-10 (proposal: orchestrator/proposals/linux-host.md; answers: PhysX OFF on Linux for now with a later PhysX-for-Linux PR, x86_64 AND arm64 eventually, host stays loopback-bound behind an SSH tunnel/proxy, the ubuntu leg becomes a required check once green (the user sets branch protection), smoke test ported to one Python script for both OSes, install X11/Vulkan dev packages for now, Dockerfile AND systemd unit). Nothing can be built locally; CI is the build. Scope (PR D): docs/editor.html section on running the host on Linux (packages, build, loopback bind behind an SSH tunnel or reverse proxy, --token-env, --tls and the certificate directory, systemd stdin is /dev/null so never pass --exit-on-stdin-eof there, firewall guidance); deploy/n2editorhost.service (systemd, hardened: dedicated user or DynamicUser, StateDirectory for the TLS identity and project, NoNewPrivileges, token via EnvironmentFile or LoadCredential); deploy/Dockerfile (multi-stage, build with the apt list, minimal runtime image, non-root, volume for the project and the TLS identity, binds loopback by default with a documented override). Nothing here runs in CI: list as unverified the image build and the systemd unit on a real machine; if a docker build step can be added to CI cheaply, do it. Context update (2026-10-11): #113 #114 #115 #116 merged. Build recipe to document and put in the Dockerfile: Ubuntu 24.04, the apt packages from the tests.yml linux job, Clang 20 from apt.llvm.org with libstdc++ 14 via --gcc-install-dir (copy the exact steps from the `linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)` job; GCC-built hosts are unsupported until the sol2 same-signature-lambda bug is fixed), PhysX OFF on Linux for now (a separate PhysX-for-Linux item follows), arm64 builds scalar-only (no NEON). The Dockerfile must build on both x86_64 and arm64 (buildx multi-arch is fine, no CI publish needed). The host binary is build/bin/N2EditorHost; it binds 127.0.0.1 by default (check HostOptions for the bind option; if none exists, document that and do NOT add one in this item: report it as needsUser if the Docker use case needs one, since a container needs 0.0.0.0 inside plus a published loopback port). User data/TLS identity: $XDG_DATA_HOME/n2engine or $HOME/.local/share/n2engine, no HOME means --tls refuses (PR #114): the systemd unit and the Dockerfile must set HOME or XDG_DATA_HOME/StateDirectory. Also fix the open low from linux-arm64: docs/testing.html ~line 290 says the TLS smoke test runs only on the Windows TLS ON leg and the Linux Clang leg; the arm64 Clang leg runs it too. Mention the required check name `linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)` where CI is described.
acceptance: Docs, unit and Dockerfile present and consistent with the host options
notes: Draft. Hardening for exposed hosts (per-user tokens, rate limiting, read-only mode) stays deferred and is mentioned as such.
